research_rationale:
EO 11202 (Mar. 5, 1965; 30 FR 3185) directed that a Schedule B Student Trainee in a shortage occupation be converted to a career or career-conditional appointment if four conditions were met (Sec. 1 items (1)-(4)), defined a cooperative work-study program (Sec. 2) and told the Civil Service Commission to prescribe regulations (Sec. 3). Section 4 of EO 11813 (signed Oct. 7, 1974; 39 FR 36317) states "Executive Order No. 11202 of March 5, 1965, is hereby revoked." and Section 5 states "This order shall become effective immediately." The order is a standing conversion rule with no term of its own, so the express revocation is its first and only end: all four dossier clauses end together on 1974-10-07. The cross-check is the held 5 U.S.C. 3301 note in jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t5-s3301.txt, which states that Executive Order No. 11202 "was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 11813, Oct. 7, 1974, 39 F.R. 36317". No earlier end was found: the only later-event records are EO 11813 (revocation) and the U.S. Code note citing it.

savings.reason: Conversions to career or career-conditional appointments completed under Section 1 before Oct. 7, 1974 were executed acts. EO 11813 Section 4 revokes EO 11202 without any language undoing them, and no held source shows a continuing independent command. Appointments already made survive as accrued status; the conversion authority itself ended on 1974-10-07.
